validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed, high tier, 3 independent Russian-language sources, all verified live and all naming this pipeline explicitly (not the sheet's own generic list-page trap): (1) kun.uz, Dec 26 2020 — reports capital repair completed and hydrostatic testing begun on a section of the 'Келиф-Мубарек' pipeline in Kashkadarya region (verified: contains 'Келиф-Мубарек'); (2) mineral.ru, Sep 4 2003 (Interfax wire, republished by a mining-industry outlet) — 'previously gas was transported to south Uzbekistan (Surkhandarya, south Kashkadarya) via the Kelif-Dushanbe and Kelif-Mubarek pipelines, significant sections of which run through Turkmen territory' (verified: contains 'Келиф-Мубарек'; cert chain unverified but page confirmed live); (3) RIA Novosti, Jan 14 2003 — reports a planned intergovernmental agreement to transfer sections of the 'main transit gas pipeline Mubarek-Kelif and Kelif-Dushanbe' to Turkmenistan, negotiated by TM deputy PM Elly Gurbanmuradov and UZ first deputy PM K. Tuleganov in Turkmenabat (verified: contains 'Мубарек-Келиф'). Background (search-only, not cited): multiple Russian outlets independently describe this as the Soviet-era Khoja-Gugerdag(Afghanistan)-Kelif-Mubarek line, originally built to import Afghan gas to the USSR, reversed after ~1990 to export Turkmen/Uzbek gas toward Afghanistan. This is a real, well-documented, historically significant transboundary trunk. CLASSIFICATION: Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission are correct in substance — every independent source calls it a 'magistral'nyy transitnyy gazoprovod' (main transit gas pipeline). DUPLICATE: not a duplicate of anything on the 18-row roster. mineral.ru explicitly names Kelif-Dushanbe (P6937) and Kelif-Mubarek (P6936) as two separate lines sharing a Kelif origin — same-corridor-different-destination, real pipe, not a double count. Also distinct in name and role from the Mubarek-Zirabulak family (P6933-P6935, a different corridor entirely) and the Mubarek-Kagan family (P6965/P6966).

Exactly the wiki-citation trap flagged in scope guidance: 18 rows map to 11 gem.wiki pages, and this URL was harvested onto the wrong row. The Fuel=Gas / PipelineType=transmission values themselves are correct on the merits (see existence entry above), so this is a citation-pointer defect, not a data error — but the cited source does not actually support what it is attached to. kun.uz (already verified, already used for Status/Location [ref] on this same row) directly names Kelif-Mubarek and is transport-infrastructure content, so it is a clean substitute; proposing it here rather than silently carrying the mis-citation forward.

validity.researcher_notes: Current Owner [ref] cites two URLs for Owner1=Uztransgaz / Owner2=Turkmengaz: utg.uz/ru/about/history/ (genuine 404, matches the country-wide known issue) and mfa.gov.tm/en/articles/84. I fetched mfa.gov.tm directly: it is Turkmenistan's own official list of its 'main gas pipelines' (11 named: TM-UZ-KZ-China, Nayip-Deryalyk, Dowletabat-Deryalyk, Bukhara-Ural, Ekerem-Bekdash, Korpeje-Kurtkui, Dovletabad-Sarahs-Hangeran, East-West, TAPI, Trans-Caspian, Fourth Branch D) and Kelif-Mubarek is NOT among them — url_verifier confirms the page does not contain 'Kelif' or 'Mubarek'. So the existing ref does not actually support the Turkmengaz co-ownership claim; it is a generic/aggregate citation of the kind flagged as an existence-adjacent problem in scope guidance (here it's an attribution problem specifically, since existence is independently well-established elsewhere). I also found the RIA Novosti Jan-2003 wire (see existence entry) reporting that a transfer of Turkmen-territory SECTIONS of this pipeline to Turkmenistan was only being NEGOTIATED as of early 2003 ('may be signed this spring') — I found no independent confirmation the transfer was ever finalized, so Turkmenistan's exact current ownership share/structure is genuinely uncertain rather than a settled fact. Uztransgaz as Owner1/Operator is a reasonable default (it is Uzbekistan's national gas-transmission monopoly and the domestic segment plainly falls in its network) but I could not find a source naming Uztransgaz specifically for THIS pipeline either — leaving Operator [ref] as UNRESOLVED below rather than force a citation. Tried re-fetching the utg.uz Wayback capture (20260314231446, the one flagged as unreadable in scope guidance) three times today (2026-08-26): still times out (curl exit 28) from this machine — consistent with the documented network condition, not new evidence the page is gone. Per standing rule, not treating this as a deletion and not citing a capture I could not read.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Newest dated independent evidence found: kun.uz, Dec 26 2020, reporting completed capital repair and started hydrostatic testing on a Kelif-Mubarek pipeline section in Kashkadarya region — i.e. active capital investment in the line barely 4 years before the sheet's LastUpdated (2024-09-10), not a sign of abandonment. Searched specifically for anything newer (2023-2026): general Uzbek gas-transport-modernization coverage exists (e.g. spot.uz Oct 2024 on a $470M modernization program involving Kazakhstan/Gazprom cooperation, utg.uz seasonal-readiness notices) but nothing names Kelif-Mubarek by name in that window. This is the expected outcome for an operating Soviet-era trunk under a state monopoly that does not routinely publish line-by-line status updates — the dormancy staleness rule (2y/4y) applies to non-operating (proposed/shelved) rows, not to an already-operating line with no adverse evidence, so 'confirm' at evidence_date 2020-12 rather than 'stale' is the correct read. No evidence of decommissioning, supersession, or reversal found; note the 2003 Shurtan-Sherabad line (P2698) took over routine southern-Uzbekistan supply so Kelif-Mubarek's traffic pattern may have changed post-2003, but multiple sources (incl. the 2020 repair) show the physical line remains maintained and in active use, consistent with Status=operating.

summary: P6936 Kelif-Mubarek: existence confirmed high (3 independent RU sources, none GEM-derived); status operating confirmed (evidence_date 2020-12, no newer status-changing evidence found); two attribution/sourcing repairs flagged (Fuel/PipelineType ref mis-points to a Mubarek-Zirabulak video, not this pipeline; Owner2=Turkmengaz ref does not actually name this pipeline and utg.uz link is a confirmed dead link whose Wayback capture stayed unreachable today); Operator [ref] left UNRESOLVED (plausible default, no source found naming it).
